questions.question: On the price board's newest day for each hub, which hub had the highest day-ahead daily mean, and what was it in USD per MWh?
questions.answer: SPP's SPPNORTH_HUB had the highest day-ahead daily mean on the price board's newest day. It was 51.72 USD/MWh (price_board_latest, derived). The row is stamped 2026-11-06T00:00Z, a day label that the tool also reads as 5 November 2026 in Central time. The next highest was CAISO's TH_NP15_GEN-APND at 51.30 USD/MWh (price_board_latest). The board's day-ahead ranking covers 11 hubs: 6 ERCOT, 3 CAISO and 2 SPP. MISO, NYISO and ISO-NE hubs are not in the table I read.

questions.question: What moved most on the price board: which hub's day-ahead daily mean changed most, in percent, on its newest day against the day before, and by how much?
questions.answer: ERCOT's HB_WEST had the largest day-ahead move on the price board. Its newest day-ahead daily mean rose 132.19 percent against the day before (price_board_latest, derived). That was an increase of 25.63 USD/MWh (price_board_latest), to a daily mean of 45.01 USD/MWh (price_board_latest). The row is stamped 2026-11-06T00:00Z (UTC), which is 6 pm Central on 5 November 2026. The next largest moves were SPPNORTH_HUB at 82.96 percent and ERCOT HB_NORTH at 79.56 percent (price_board_latest). The ranking covers 11 hubs. A hub whose rows are held is not in the table, so MISO, NYISO and ISO-NE hubs are not part of it.

questions.question: Where is the spark spread widest on the price board (each hub's newest day, at the board's stated heat rate), and what is it in USD per MWh?
questions.answer: The spark spread is widest at SPP North Hub (spp:SPPNORTH_HUB). It is 33.31 USD/MWh (price_board_spreads, derived) on the board's newest day, 6 November 2026 (UTC date label). The board's spark spread is the day-ahead daily mean minus an assumed heat rate times Henry Hub gas. The heat rate is an assumption, and the table does not state its value in the results I read. The other hubs on the board are CAISO SP15 (TH_SP15_GEN-APND) at 25.33 USD/MWh and ERCOT HB_HUBAVG at 22.23 USD/MWh, both on 6 November 2026 (price_board_spreads). Only these three hubs were in the table read.

questions.question: Which hub on the price board had the lowest real-time daily mean on its newest day, and what was it in USD per MWh?
questions.answer: ERCOT's HB_NORTH had the lowest real-time daily mean on the price board: 21.72 USD/MWh (price_board_latest, derived). This is the mean for the complete local operating day labelled 2026-11-04. The next lowest was ERCOT HB_BUSAVG at 25.33 USD/MWh (price_board_latest). The board ranks 11 hubs: 6 ERCOT, 2 SPP and 3 CAISO. The SPP hubs' newest day is only 2026-10-31. Their means were 35.21 USD/MWh (SPPSOUTH_HUB) and 37.64 USD/MWh (SPPNORTH_HUB), so neither was lower (price_board_latest). The ranking leaves out any hub whose rows are held, so it may not cover every ISO.

questions.question: On the price board, which hub's day-ahead price ran furthest from real time (day-ahead minus real time, either sign) on its newest day, and by how much in USD per MWh?
questions.answer: ERCOT's HB_WEST had the widest gap between day-ahead and real time on its newest day. Day-ahead ran 16.44 USD/MWh above real time on 2026-11-04 (price_board_latest, derived; day-ahead daily mean minus real-time daily mean, dates in UTC). Next were ERCOT HB_SOUTH at 15.28 and HB_HUBAVG at 14.77 USD/MWh. The widest negative gap was SPPNORTH_HUB at -9.02 USD/MWh on 2026-10-31, which is smaller in size. The board ranking covers 11 hubs (ERCOT, CAISO and SPP). The tool notes that a hub whose rows are held is left out of the table it reads.
